outcome: No proof, disproof, or new partial result on the specific question of odd noncototients was found; the conjecture that no odd number larger than 5 is a noncototient remains exactly where it stood in January 2024, resting on the same Goldbach-type heuristic (Browkin/Schinzel era).
summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks whether any odd noncototients exist beyond the three small known cases (1, 3, 5), each disposed of by hand (1=2-φ(2), 3=9-φ(9), 5=25-φ(25)). The standing conjecture — that no odd number greater than 5 is a noncototient — rests on the (also open) strengthened Goldbach conjecture that every even number greater than 6 is a sum of two distinct primes p and q, since then pq - φ(pq) = p+q-1 expresses that odd number as a cototient. I searched the Wikipedia article on noncototients, the OEIS sequence A005278 (noncototients) and its comments, the erdosproblems.com entry, and general web searches for any 2024-2026 proof, disproof, or partial progress specific to the odd case; none of these show any post-January-2024 activity on this specific question. The only genuinely new and AI-relevant development I found in this neighborhood is unrelated to odd noncototients: Erdős Problem #418 ('are there infinitely many noncototients?', i.e. the density/infinitude question, already answered affirmatively by Browkin and Schinzel in 1995 for even numbers of the form 2^k·509203) was formalized in Lean in late 2025 as part of the erdosproblems.com/teorth formalization project, with the author (Boris Alexeev) reporting he 'asked ChatGPT to explain the proof by Browkin and Schinzel and then Aristotle [Harmonic's AI system] to auto-formalize the resulting LaTeX file.' That is (a) about a different question (infinitude/density of noncototients in general, not the odd case), and (b) a formalization of a 1995 result, not new mathematics in the window — so under §3.1 and §6.1 it is out of scope for this bullet and does not change its status; I record it here only as context so it isn't silently lost, and so a reader isn't misled by erdosproblems.com's page for #418 which could look at a glance like it bears on this problem.
competing_reading: None. The Erdős #418 Lean/AI formalization is unambiguously about the general (even) noncototient infinitude question, not the odd-noncototient question in this bullet, and even that underlying mathematical result (Browkin-Schinzel 1995) predates the frozen revision by decades. There is no plausible reading under which either the odd-noncototient conjecture or its supporting Goldbach-type heuristic moved in the window.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or disproof of the strengthened Goldbach-type statement (or a direct argument) establishing that every odd number greater than 5 either is or is not a noncototient; short of that, any paper explicitly exhibiting or ruling out an odd noncototient greater than 5, or any update to OEIS A005278's comments/references reflecting new work.
